Adani signs $1 billion copper supply deal with recycler Attero to cut import dependence: Reuters
snippet: Adani Enterprises signs a 1 billion dollar deal with Attero to source copper anode for its Kutch Copper smelter, aiming to reduce import reliance.

read.desc: Adani Enterprises signs a 1 billion dollar deal with Attero to source copper anode for its Kutch Copper smelter, aiming to reduce import reliance.
paras: The agreement is expected to help reduce India's reliance on imported copper feedstock, which remains in short supply.

Under the arrangement, Kutch Copper will procure 2,000 metric tonnes of copper anode every month from Attero. This is expected to lower the smelter's dependence on imports by around 5%, the sources told Reuters, requesting anonymity as the details have not been made public.
The contract, signed around three months ago, is valued at approximately $1 billion at prevailing market prices, they added. The deal had not been previously reported.

Adani Enterprises began production last year at its Kutch Copper facility in Mundra, Gujarat, which has an annual capacity of 500,000 tonnes. The conglomerate is looking to double the plant's capacity, a move that would make it the world's largest single-location copper smelter.
The company's plans to secure supplies of copper feedstock have therefore drawn considerable interest from the industry. Adani did not respond to Reuters' request for comment on the agreement.

Adani’s Tarali project: The dispute over its cost and wildlife fee
snippet: Adani Green’s Tarali hydropower project is facing scrutiny after an affidavit cited a sharply lower cost, reducing the proposed wildlife conservation deposit. Maharashtra has halted work, with an ...

read.desc: Adani Green’s Tarali hydropower project is facing scrutiny after an affidavit cited a sharply lower cost, reducing the proposed wildlife conservation deposit. Maharashtra has halted work, with an inquiry pending.
paras: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB), in a letter to Adani Green Energy Ltd, has directed it to stop excavation and construction work linked to its Tarali hydropower project in Satara district.

It said the “excavation/development work” at Sawarghar village was done without permission from the MPCB and without obtaining environmental clearance. The company has said these are construction-support facilities and do not form part of the permanent project components, which “have the requisite statutory clearances”.
This comes amid the controversy over Adani Green’s affidavit regarding the cost of the 1,500 MW Pumped Storage Project (PSP), proposed on the Tarali dam reservoir.

The Indian Express reported that the renewable energy company ow­ned by the Adani Group had sought to sharply revise the declared cost of its 1,500 MW hydropower project to Rs 56.75 crore from Rs 5,675 crore. This revision proportionally reduced the amount the company was required to deposit towards wildlife conservation and protection to Rs 2.27 crore, from Rs 227 crore.
The project spans 150.74 hectares of non-forest land in Nivade, Tondoshi, Kalambe and Jalu villages in Patan taluka of Maharashtra’s Satara district.

paras: HCL's Shiv Nadar and family retained their title as the country's most generous in 2026, donating Rs 2,593 crore for various social causes, a report said on Friday.

Among the richest Indians, Gautam Adani and family witnessed a 127 per cent jump in giving to Rs 877 crore, while Mukesh Ambani's outgo slipped by 1 per cent to Rs 620 crore to rank fourth among givers, the report by Hurun India and EdelGive said.
The Bajaj family retained its third place on the list with a 42 per cent jump in donations to Rs 632 crore, the report said.
The EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List 2026 features 219 philanthropists who together donated Rs 11,554 crore in FY26, up 11 per cent from Rs 10,380 crore a year earlier.

Hurun India's founder and chief researcher Anas Rahman Junaid said amid concerns about a K-shaped economy, the question is how this prosperity can create wider opportunity and added that the list documents that journey.

New data centre cable business helps Diamond Power reduce reliance on Adani Group
snippet: The early traction marks a significant step in the Diamond Power’s efforts to diversify beyond the Adani Group, which has dominated its order book.

read.desc: The early traction marks a significant step in the Diamond Power’s efforts to diversify beyond the Adani Group, which has dominated its order book.
paras: Mumbai: Diamond Power Infrastructure Ltd’s new data centre cable business generated ₹ 242 crore in revenue in its first month of operations, accounting for a fourth of its July-September revenue. The early traction marks a significant step in the company’s efforts to diversify beyond the Adani Group, which has dominated its order book.

The company began supplying cables from its newly commissioned copper cable line in September, just a month after raising ₹ 1,614 crore through a qualified institutional placement (QIP), its management said during its 4 November earnings call. Its copper cable manufacturing capacity currently stands at 1,500 tonnes a month, which it plans to increase to 2,500 tonnes.

"The QIP funds came into the company in August. In September, the very next month, we achieved record production of ₹ 575 crores. Of that, our team made and delivered ₹ 242 crores of data centre cables in a single month," Amit Bhatnagar, head of corporate strategy at Diamond Power, told analysts in its 4 November earnings call.

The cables were delivered to data centre engineering, procurement, and construction contractors like L&T , AurionPro, Sterling and Wilson, and Blue Star, he said. The new business helped the Gujarat-based cable and conductor manufacturer more than double its quarterly revenue year-on-year to ₹ 1,032 crore.

The quick start comes as companies in the data centre supply chain are banking on a growing opportunity as India builds more facilities to meet demand for cloud computing and artificial intelligence. Around 3,860 megawatts (MW) of new data centre capacity is planned or under construction through 2030, according to a September report by real estate consultancy Cushman & Wakefield.

title: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani's scrapped Kenya power deal carries $339 million exit bill
snippet: Kenya's Treasury estimates it could pay Sh43.94 billion to exit Gautam Adani's cancelled power-line deal, more than the two lines were meant to cost.

read.desc: Kenya's Treasury estimates it could pay Sh43.94 billion to exit Gautam Adani's cancelled power-line deal, more than the two lines were meant to cost.
paras: Indian billionaire Gautam Adani's cancelled power-line deal in Kenya could cost the country Sh43.94 billion ($339 million) to unwind, two years after President William Ruto ordered it scrapped.

The estimate appears in the National Treasury's fifth annual report on the state of public-private partnerships in Kenya, covering the year to June 2026. It is the termination payment linked to the contract between Adani Energy Solutions Ltd. and the state-owned Kenya Electricity Transmission Co., known as Ketraco.
The report describes the sum as a contingent liability rather than an amount due immediately. It does not break the figure down or disclose the costs Adani has submitted for verification.

Adani Energy Solutions signed the 30-year deal with Ketraco in October 2024 to build, finance and run power lines and substations. The wider agreement was valued at Sh95.68 billion ($739 million). The two lines named in the termination estimate, the 400-kilovolt Lessos-Loosuk line and the 220-kilovolt Kisumu (Kibos)-Kakamega-Musaga line, were expected to cost about Sh41 billion ($317 million) together.
That puts the estimated exit payment about Sh3 billion above the cost of building the two lines.

snippet: Adani Airport Holdings raised ₹2,790 crore from 360 ONE Asset, bringing its external equity funding to ₹12,615 crore. The capital will support airport upgrades, city-side developments, and other ...

read.desc: Adani Airport Holdings raised  ₹2,790 crore from 360 ONE Asset, bringing its external equity funding to  ₹12,615 crore. The capital will support airport upgrades, city-side developments, and other non-aero revenues as the operator aims at annual passenger capacity of 200 million at eight airports.
paras: New Delhi/Mumbai: The ₹ 2,790 crore ($300 million) equity funding raise announced by Adani Airport Holdings Ltd (AAHL), the airport unit of Adani Enterprises Ltd, on Monday will help the company speed up the development of its non-aeronautical revenue, funding the development of city-side infrastructure like hotels.

The airport operator said that it has signed a binding agreement with 360 ONE Asset, which will acquire up to a 1.55% stake, taking its total external equity fundraise to date to ₹ 12,615 crore (about $1.35 billion).
AAHL manages eight airports — Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Lucknow, Guwahati, Mangaluru and Thiruvananthapuram — and serves more than 23% of India's total passenger traffic.
The funding comes as AAHL looks to finance an ambitious city-side expansion program and strengthen its balance sheet ahead of India’s fresh round of airport privatization anticipated to begin soon.

“We are committed to developing a complete ecosystem around our airports by transforming them from simple transit hubs into vibrant airport cities that merge aviation, commerce, leisure, and regional logistics…,” Jeet Adani, non-executive director, AAHL said in a statement.

New Delhi: Adani Defence & Aerospace has successfully demonstrated its Bagheera AT1 anti-tank guided missile (ATGM) system at the Pokhran Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan.
The vehicle-mounted missile system demonstrated day-and-night targeting, tandem missile firing and aerial-target engagement capabilities.

With an anti-armour engagement range of up to 8 km, Bagheera AT1 represents an important step in India’s efforts to strengthen domestic defence manufacturing and develop advanced weapons for the Indian Armed Forces .
The demonstration was conducted on November 20, 2026, at the Pokhran Field Firing Ranges in Rajasthan.

Adani Airports raises ~USD 300 million primary equity from 360 ONE Asset
snippet: Adani Airports raises $300 million from 360 ONE Asset to expand infrastructure, airport cities, and non-aeronautical services.

read.desc: Adani Airports raises $300 million from 360 ONE Asset to expand infrastructure, airport cities, and non-aeronautical services.
paras: Newsroom Media Releases Adani Airports raises ~USD 300 million primary equity from 360 ONE Asset Adani Airports raises ~USD 300 million primary equity from 360 ONE Asset Fresh equity takes Adani Airport Holdings Limited’s total raise to ~USD 1.35 billion Editor’s Synopsis:

Ahmedabad, 23 November 2026 : Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL), a subsidiary of Adani Enterprises Limited (AEL) and one of India's largest private airport operators, has entered into a binding agreement with 360 ONE Alternates Asset Management Limited, acting through its funds and affiliates (360 ONE Asset), to raise ₹2,790 crores (~ USD 300 million), taking its total equity raise to ~USD 1.35 billion so far.

The transaction builds on an earlier round of ₹9,825 crores (~USD 1 billion) of primary equity capital from a consortium of leading domestic and global investors including Alpha Wave Global, Premji Invest, Temasek and BlackRock managed funds. This represented one of the largest primary equity investments from financial institutions in India’s airport infrastructure sector.

“This partnership is yet another milestone in building out the Adani Airports platform. Having such marquee, long-term investors on board is a testament to their confidence in India’s aviation growth story,” said Mr. Jeet Adani, Non-Executive Director, Adani Airport Holdings Limited . “We are committed to developing a complete ecosystem around our airports by transforming them from simple transit hubs into vibrant airport cities that merge aviation, commerce, leisure, and regional logistics to drive sustained national growth,” he added.

The fresh round, which brings 360 ONE Asset alongside Alpha Wave Global, Premji Invest, Temasek and BlackRock managed funds, reflects the institutional endorsement of AAHL’s scale, operating capabilities and long-term growth potential.

Adani Airports Taps Rs 2,790 Cr Equity To Scale Passenger Capacity To 200 Mn
snippet: Adani Airports raises Rs 2,790 crore from 360 ONE at an USD 18 billion valuation as it targets 200 million annual passenger capacity.

read.desc: Adani Airports raises Rs 2,790 crore from 360 ONE at an USD 18 billion valuation as it targets 200 million annual passenger capacity.
paras: Adani Airport Holdings (AAHL) has entered into an agreement with 360 ONE Alternates Asset Management for a Rs 2,790 crore primary equity investment, strengthening its capital base as it pursues a substantial expansion of aviation infrastructure and airport-linked commercial assets.

The transaction values AAHL at a pre-money valuation of about USD 18 billion and takes the airport operator’s aggregate equity mobilisation to approximately USD 1.35 billion. AAHL will issue fresh shares to 360 ONE Asset at the same valuation and on the same terms agreed with investors that participated in its preceding capital raise.

The latest investment follows the Rs 9,825 crore equity infusion announced earlier this year by a consortium comprising Alpha Wave Global, Premji Invest, Temasek and funds managed by BlackRock. The transaction marked AAHL’s first major institutional equity raise from a group of global investors.

The earlier investors committed the capital through a three-tranche arrangement. Upon completion of that transaction, the investors are expected to hold a collective 5.54 per cent stake in AAHL. With 360 ONE Asset joining the shareholder group, investors participating in the two transactions are expected to hold an aggregate stake of approximately 7.01 per cent in AAHL.

Expansion Remains Capital Priority The successive equity transactions come as AAHL undertakes a broad-based expansion of its airport portfolio. The company is targeting annual passenger-handling capacity of 200 million, compared with its historical capacity of around 96 million. The capital will support the expansion and modernisation of airport facilities, alongside investments in infrastructure required to accommodate rising passenger volumes.
